documents.unit: Office of Academic Integrity, Undergraduate Education
documents.title: Academic Integrity and Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: Faculty-facing guidance from the academic integrity office. It frames unauthorized AI use as a possible integrity violation and advises instructors on assignment design, setting and communicating their own AI rules, and handling suspected misuse without relying on detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university rule on whether students may use AI; it tells instructors to "set clear guidelines and expectations" and to act "if you do not want students using them", leaving the decision to each instructor, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: Framing sentence: "may be used in a productive, creative, and educational manner, or they can be used to cheat", so it sets the institution-level principle that AI has both legitimate and illicit uses; coded as a general framework statement (P56), informative.
units.anchor: AI tools may be used in a productive, creative, and educational manner
units.frag_start: AI tools may be used in

units.why: States that "unauthorized use of such tools... could be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy", classifying unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36); applies to everyone, in the misuse phase.
units.anchor: which could be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy
units.frag_end: violation of the academic integrity policy

units.why: Points to the Howe Center and Center for Teaching Excellence resources; this is support for faculty learning about AI and assignment design (P63) rather than a student rule.
units.anchor: have published information and resources about AI tools as they pertain to teaching

units.why: "Learn how ChatGPT and other tools ... work. Use them yourself." advises instructors to learn the tools before setting policy, matching P63 (faculty learning AI) rather than P59, which concerns instructors using AI for their own teaching work.
units.anchor: Use them yourself.
units.frag_start: Learn how ChatGPT and other tools

units.why: "Think about how the tools might be used creatively in your course" encourages instructors to build AI use into teaching (demonstrating pros and cons, critique), which fits P44 (courses teach or demonstrate AI use).
units.anchor: Think about how the tools might be used creatively in your course.

units.why: Instructors are told to "minimize the opportunity to use AI tools or use them successfully": assignment redesign around AI (P35), conditioned on the instructor not wanting AI use.
units.anchor: creating assignments that minimize the opportunity to use AI tools or use them successfully
units.frag_end: if you do not want students using them

units.why: The parenthetical "(if you do not want students using them)" shows each instructor decides whether students may use AI, which is P04, not a university-wide default.
units.anchor: if you do not want students using them
units.frag_end: if you do not want students using them
units.policy: The guidance leaves it to each instructor whether students may use AI tools.

units.why: "If allowing use of text-generating tools, require citations as you would for any source" sets a disclosure/citation expectation for instructors who allow AI (P24).
units.anchor: If allowing use of text-generating tools, require citations as you would for any source.
units.frag_end: as you would for any source

units.why: "Have discussions with your students about the use of AI text/answer/product generating tools" tells instructors to communicate about AI use; closest type is P09 (state AI expectations to students), chosen over P04 because it concerns communication.
units.anchor: Have discussions with your students about the use of AI

units.why: "Set clear guidelines and expectations - explain why you have these guidelines" asks instructors to state and justify their AI rules, i.e. communicating expectations (P09).
units.anchor: Set clear guidelines and expectations

units.why: "Include your specific guidelines in course syllabi and assignment instructions" is the syllabus-statement requirement (P09), phrased as an instruction to instructors.
units.anchor: Include your specific guidelines in course syllabi and assignment instructions.

units.why: "Provide resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing and summarizing, and citation" asks instructors to support students' source-use skills; no type covers instructors teaching citation skills, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Provide resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing and summarizing, and citation.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors provide students resources on appropriate source use, paraphrasing, summarizing and citation.

units.why: "Have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing with an emphasis on understanding" is a teaching activity to build skills AI could bypass; it fits no type directly (not an assessment redesign nor a student rule), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing with an emphasis on understanding
units.uncovered_note: Instructors have students practice paraphrasing and summarizing, emphasizing understanding and explaining content over rewording.

units.why: "Discuss the purpose of course assignments" is a communication step so students see why work should be their own; it states no type's rule directly, so UNCOVERED rather than stretching P41.
units.anchor: Discuss the purpose of course assignments.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors discuss the purpose of course assignments with students.

units.why: Instructors should "Generate output for your assignments to use as comparison to student work": using AI output as evidence to identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: Generate output for your assignments to use as comparison to student work.

units.why: "Review sources (some AI tools fabricate sources)" is an instructor check for misuse using evidence in the submission, P40; P31 is about students verifying output so does not fit.
units.anchor: Review sources (some AI tools fabricate sources).

units.why: "Select specific sources/content/choices to follow-up on with students in a conversation" tells instructors to talk with students before escalating (P57).
units.anchor: follow-up on with students in a conversation

units.why: "Online AI Detection programs exist, but they are not well-tested and may not be accurate" warns against relying on detectors (P39).
units.anchor: they are not well-tested and may not be accurate

units.why: Instructors who "suspect Academic Dishonesty" are told to contact the Assistant Director for Academic Integrity; a route into the integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: If you suspect Academic Dishonesty or have questions about whether an issue

documents.unit: Department of Computer Science and Software Engineering
documents.title: CSE Academic Integrity Guidelines
documents.summary: A departmental integrity page whose only AI content is two bullets in a list of acceptable and unacceptable practices for problem-solving assignments. Generative AI is allowed within the limits each instructor sets per assignment and counts as unacceptable otherwise.
documents.stance_why: Generative AI is "acceptable" only "within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor for the individual assignment" and unacceptable "when not explicitly approved"; the department sets no limits itself and defers to the instructor, with a restrictive fallback, so delegates.

units.why: "To learn to solve problems you must solve the problems and write your solutions independently" gives the skill-building rationale for the problem-solving rules that the AI bullets sit in (P41), stated as a must.
units.anchor: you must solve the problems and write your solutions independently.
units.frag_start: The purpose of a problem solving

units.why: Under "Acceptable", generative AI is allowed only "within the boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor for the individual assignment", so each instructor/assignment decides (P04) and AI is permitted with conditions.
units.anchor: boundaries and limitations that have been explicitly set forth by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Use of Generative AI tools such as
units.policy: Use of Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Bing, Bard, DALL-E, GitHub Copilot, etc. is acceptable within the boundaries and limitations explicitly set forth by the course instructor for the individual assignment.

units.why: Under "Unacceptable", AI use "when not explicitly approved by the course instructor" is ruled out, a fallback rule that silence means no (P06).
units.anchor: using Generative AI tools when not explicitly approved by the course instructor
units.frag_start: Use of Generative AI tools such as
units.frag_end: explicitly approved by the course instructor
units.policy: Use of Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Bing, Bard, DALL-E, GitHub Copilot, etc without meeting the explicit requirements set forth by the course instructor, or when not explicitly approved by the course instructor, is unacceptable.

notes: Coder B. The university page has no student-facing rules; all units are instructor guidance. Three units are UNCOVERED (instructors providing source-use resources, paraphrasing practice, discussing assignment purpose). CSE page: non-AI integrity rules were skipped.
